pages.text: $(li)Export Interfaces are the safer way to link subnets; Subnet Proxies can cause TPS lag, force updates and wrong reporting.

$(li)Inbound/Outbound in the Subnet Proxy UI is defined from the Terminal’s perspective: $(o)Outbound$() = main → subnet, $(o)Inbound$() = subnet → main.$(li)The directional arrow icon only appears on the top face; side faces never show it.
$(li)Point the proxy from the smaller (subnet) to the larger (main) network.

$(li)Never let a proxy both expose and accept the same item from the main network—this can cause infinite recursion and server stalls.$(li)Give each subnet unique partitions, or items/fluids get counted twice on the main network.

$(li)Verify all proxies in a subnet show a purple ring; missing rings mean broken connections that may stall the server.$(li)Copy partition/filter settings from a Storage Bus and paste them into a Subnet Proxy to save time.$(li)Cell Terminal supports subnet proxy filtering and overview;
it treats proxies as storage buses for search and IO.
$(l)Prevent event storms and lag$()$(li)Even insert-only storage buses send events into the subnet—this can trigger loops and force updates if cycles exist.

$(li)Use star topology: subnets talk directly via subnet proxies, and the main network only extracts from them (never inserts without careful filtering).$(li)Proxies reduce lag only if events are filtered at the proxy boundary; otherwise, propagation grows exponentially with depth and device count.
$(li)Large unfiltered subnets can exceed packet limits and disconnect you when opening a Cell Terminal. Reduce subnet size or filter content.
